answer: Filling 21 aliases thus needs 21 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. Because the shale index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the saffron audit republishes the digest set at close. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a kernel index of commitments rather than against the text alone. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
